title: The Caliph al-Hakim and the Merchant
logline: A caliph stops at a garden for a drink of water, is given an instant feast for his whole procession, learns it is only the owner's ordinary day, and repays the welcome with the year's entire mint of dirhams.
moral: Generous hospitality, given without calculation, can bring a reward far beyond anything expected: one cup of water became 3,700,000 dirhams.
tone: Warm, bright comedy of amazement. The humour comes from scale and speed (things appearing by the hundred) and from the owner's calm against the caliph's growing astonishment. No villain, no danger; the ending is generous and a little wry.

beats.summary: The caliph rides out in a great procession.
He asks a man in a garden for a drink of water; the man runs to serve him. The cup is planted for the ending.
Invited to rest, the caliph agrees and enters the garden.
Servants appear from nowhere with rugs and cushions for everyone.
The food multiplies: a hundred of each kind.
The caliph suspects the owner knew he was coming.
He did not: this is simply the daily routine of his house.
A hundred women of the household each send food, drink and comforts every day.
The caliph grasps how rich this man must be, and his wonder grows.
He thanks God for the prosperity of one of his subjects.
He orders the year's minted dirhams brought: 3,700,000.
He gives it all to the merchant: hospitality deserves even more.
He rides home; a short stop for water became a gift nobody expected.

subtitles.ar: خرج الخليفة الحاكم بأمر الله يومًا في موكب كبير،|ومر ببستان جميل تحيط به الأشجار.|رأى رجلًا جالسًا فيه مع خدمه،|فطلب منه شربة ماء، فأسرع الرجل وقدّم له ما يشرب.
subtitles.en: Caliph al-Hakim rode in a great procession|past a beautiful garden.|He saw a man among his servants|and asked for water, which the man readily provided.

subtitles.ar: دعا صاحب البستان الخليفة إلى النزول والاستراحة،|فوافق ودخل مع من رافقه.|وفجأة ظهر الخدم يحملون سجادًا ووسائد كثيرة،|ويجهزون للضيوف أماكن واسعة للجلوس تحت الأشجار.
subtitles.en: The garden’s owner invited the caliph to rest.|He accepted,|and attendants quickly spread many rugs and cushions|beneath the trees for his entourage.

subtitles.ar: ثم جاءت أطباق الفاكهة والحلوى، وأوعية الشراب البارد، وألوان كثيرة من الطعام.|بلغ عدد بعض هذه الأشياء مئة من كل نوع،|حتى تعجب الخليفة من سرعة تجهيز مائدة بهذا الحجم.
subtitles.en: Platters of fruit and sweets, cool drinks and food|followed—some items numbering a hundred each.|The caliph wondered how such an enormous feast had appeared so quickly.

subtitles.ar: سأل الحاكم صاحب البستان إن كان يعلم مسبقًا بمرور الموكب،|وأعد كل ذلك انتظارًا له.|أجاب الرجل أنه لم يسمع بخبر الزيارة،|وأن ما يراه الخليفة جزء من نظام بيته اليومي المعتاد.
subtitles.en: Al-Hakim asked whether the merchant had expected his visit|and prepared in advance.|The host insisted|that he had known nothing of it.

subtitles.ar: وأوضح التاجر أن في بيته مئة جارية،|وأن كل واحدة ترسل كل يوم طعامًا وشرابًا وأشياء للاستراحة.|وعندما نزل الخليفة جمع الخدم ما يأتي عادة من الجميع،|وقدموه للزائرين.
subtitles.en: The merchant explained that a hundred women in his household|each sent daily food, drink and furnishings.|His servants had simply gathered the usual contributions|for the visitors.

subtitles.ar: لم يكن القصد إقامة وليمة خاصة،|بل إن المائدة التي رآها الخليفة|كانت مما يصل إلى صاحب البستان في يوم عادي.|ازداد الحاكم دهشة عندما فهم مقدار المال الذي يستطيع هذا التاجر أن ينفقه.
subtitles.en: It was no specially arranged banquet:|the lavish spread|was part of an ordinary day.|The caliph was even more astonished by the merchant’s wealth and hospitality.

subtitles.ar: شكر الخليفة الله على ما رأى من سعة رزق أحد رعيته،|ثم أمر بإحضار ما جمع في خزينة الدولة من دراهم ضُربت في تلك السنة،|وكان عددها ثلاثة ملايين وسبعمئة ألف درهم.
subtitles.en: The caliph thanked God for the prosperity of one of his subjects.|He ordered the treasury to bring the dirhams minted|that year—three million seven hundred thousand.

subtitles.ar: أعطى الخليفة المال كله إلى التاجر،|وقال إن كرم الضيافة يستحق أكثر من ذلك.|ثم ركب جواده وعاد إلى قصره،|وبقيت زيارة الماء القصيرة سببًا في هدية لم يتوقعها صاحب البستان.
subtitles.en: He gave all the money to the merchant,|declaring such hospitality deserved even more,|and rode away.|A simple request for water had brought an extraordinary gift.

new_assets.name: orchard
new_assets.description: Walled fruit garden in two views. 'road': 2200-wide roadside strip with the low wall (top y 820), gate x 1500..1680 and six trees. 'inside': 1000-wide lawn under three trees with the gate in the back wall and tree trunks that occlude. The name is the planned orchard (AN-038); this is the walled-garden dressing of it (wall, gate, lawn, no trellis). Reusable for any garden, picnic or roadside-estate story.
new_assets.implementation: Library/sets file with orchard(ctx, o) returning anchors {ground, wall {top}, gate {x0, x1, top, cx}, trees [{x, crown}], seat, jugStand, house}. Bake the static layer per option set with bake(); trees from the existing tree() with a fruit-dot pass (seeded K.rng); wall as K.rect with halftone shade; gate from townDoor / townArchPts; sky from sky() or skyCycle(u); far city from townFarCity. front: true redraws wall or trunks over the cast.

new_assets.name: carpetRoll
new_assets.description: A rug 420 x 120 (on the lawn as a flat parallelogram, skew 30) with unroll 0..1: at 0 a roll (ellipse end r 26 with a spiral, length 120) that can be carried on a shoulder; as unroll grows the flat part extends from the start edge and the roll shrinks and travels; fringe at both ends; col and border options, pattern none / diamonds.
new_assets.implementation: One function carpetRoll(ctx, x, y, {w, d, unroll, col, border, pattern, dir}). Flat part: polygon clipped to unroll * w with a border stroke and a row of diamonds; roll: ellipse plus 2-turn spiral, radius 26 * (1 - 0.6 * unroll); ripple = 3 px sine on the leading 60 px while moving.

new_assets.name: feastSpread
new_assets.description: Counts made visible: n (0..100) small dish icons of one kind laid out ten per row in a receding grid (row scale 1 -> 0.55, row pitch 34 -> 20), popping in order with a 2-frame stagger; returns the grid box so a counter tag can be attached. Kinds reuse the foodTray contents at icon size plus jug and cushion.
new_assets.implementation: feastSpread(ctx, x, y, t, {kind, n, t0, w}) loops i < n, pos from row/col with the perspective scale, each icon scaled by K.beat pop from t0 + i * 0.066; icons are the foodTray(kind) drawing at s 0.28 (bake one icon per kind and drawImage it 100 times).

new_assets.name: hundredWindows
new_assets.description: Diagram of a great house: facade 700 x 630 with crenellations and a door, a ten by ten grid of windows (46 x 40, pitch 64 x 58). Fields: rise 0..1, lit 0..100 (diagonal order), busts (list of window indices that show a waving person bust), send: [[t0, kind]...] (every window emits one icon that drops to the door along a bezier and leaves along the ground to the right), highlight (index, ring). Reusable for any "a hundred rooms / many households / everyone sends" explanation.
new_assets.implementation: Bake the facade; windows as townWindow-style rects, lit colour by index order (row + col diagonal) against lit. Busts: person drawn at s 0.22 clipped to the window rect. Icons: baked 28 px tray / jug / cushion sprites moved by K.bezier with a per-window delay from K.rng(seed + i) (pure function of t). Stream on the ground: icons continue x += speed * (t - tDoor).

new_assets.name: person costume preset 'guard'
new_assets.description: The planned guard preset (AN-086 and others): pointed helmet with neck cloth, short tunic, sash, optional moustache; hold:'spear' (shaft 300, leaf blade) with an optional pennant. Blue tunics here.
new_assets.implementation: Add 'guard' to the COSTUME table in Library/cast/people.js (helmet = triangle over a half ellipse plus a cloth polygon behind the neck); spear as a hold option drawn through the hand like hold:'stick', pennant = a triangle driven by swing().

new_assets.name: goblet, waterJug, floorCushion, foodTray (kind option), chest, coinPile
new_assets.description: Small props already planned by other films, reused under their planned names; the only extension is the foodTray kind option (fruit, sweets, rice, bread, dome) and a silver palette on coinPile for dirhams.
new_assets.implementation: One function per prop in Library/props (things.js style) with a registry entry; flat shapes with a halftone shade side and one highlight. Chest: box 120 x 90 with a lid polygon rotating about the back edge by open; coins as a yellow-white mound with 5 coin ellipses on top.

new_assets.name: goldGlow, inset circle
new_assets.description: The planned treasure light (rays, halftone disc, staggered star glints, strength 0..1) on the vault, the chests and the thought-cloud pile; the planned round picture-in-picture with an iris for the window close-up (S9) and the two-second dismount replay (S10).
new_assets.implementation: As planned by the other films: goldGlow(ctx, x, y, r, t, {strength}) with K.dots disc and tapered ray polygons; inset(ctx, x, y, r, p, draw) = circular clip with a black brush ring, p drives the iris radius.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: P4 English ("The host insisted that he had known nothing of it.") leaves out the second half of the Arabic (that what the caliph sees is part of the normal daily routine of his house); both are kept verbatim and the picture follows the Arabic.

SCRIPT: smaller differences kept verbatim: P1 English omits "surrounded by trees"; P6 English adds "and hospitality"; P8 English omits "returned to his palace" and "that the garden's owner had not expected".

The hundred "جارية" of P5 are shown neutrally as women of the household at the windows of a house diagram (three small waving busts in maiden / lady costume, the rest as lit windows), matching the English "a hundred women in his household"; default: this neutral staging.

A vizier, four guards and a child servant are added as the "procession" and the "servants" the script mentions, with light comedy (the vizier and the sweets, the cushion tower, the caught orange); default: included.

For "ضُربت في تلك السنة" the plan adds a short treasury scene with a stamp hammer striking three coins and a counter rolling to 3,700,000; the script only says the caliph ordered the money brought. Default: included.
The caliph thanking God is staged as raised palms, eyes lifted then closed, light through the leaves and the company lowering their heads; default: this respectful, simple staging with no lettering.
Caliph al-Hakim is drawn as the generic Library caliph (crowned turban, red robe, grey beard), not as a likeness of the historical ruler; default: generic storybook caliph.

The supplied English subtitles contain em dashes in P3 and P7 ("followed—some", "year—three") while the series rule forbids em dashes in on-screen text; default: keep the supplied text verbatim in the subtitles.

English lettering added beyond the script: AHH!, FLUMP!, BRRR!, 100!, DID YOU KNOW?, NO IDEA!, CLINK!, ALL OF IT!, AND MORE!, plus labels such as ONE CUP OF WATER and 3,700,000 DIRHAMS (Western digits); default: included.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; cues from timing.json words (w(p, n)); every action above carries the exact word and its start time. Anticipation may start up to 0.4 s before the cue; contacts land on the cue.

World 1000 x 1230 for the garden interior, house diagram and treasury; the road view is a 2200 strip drawn with ctx.translate(-camX, 0). Ground y 900 everywhere. Use the template camAt clamp and panel-only shake (none is needed here except a 3 px tick on the chest thump at 151.9).

Set LIFE.t = t every frame so all figures blink; add explicit noBlink for the held shocks (59.0-60.2, 74.56-74.94, 153.6-154.0). Every figure always has a gaze target: use look()/gazePlan for the caliph and the owner, lookAt for the listeners.

Riders: rideOn(ctx, 'horse', {...walk(xf, t, {stride: GAIT.horse * s}), y: 900, s, pal}, personP). Dismount and mount are swaps between rideOn and a standing person at the apex of a hop() arc, hidden partly by the horse body; do not try to animate a leg swing.
Groups never move in unison: servants and guards take stagger(i) delays of 0.1-0.3 s and different walk phases. Four servants and four guards are the same figure with pal variants.

The goblet is one object across the film: the owner takes it back at 21.0, it sits on the jug stand until the end, and he holds it from 165.3. Keep its colour (yellow with a red band) identical in S2, in the S16 balloon and in S17.

Counters use S.counter: 0..100 at 54.2-56.3 (ease-in), 0..100 at 89.4-90.5, and 0..3,700,000 from 145.4 with holds at 3,000,000 (147.7) and the final slam at 150.38. Format with commas; digits at least 90 px tall for the last one.

Thought clouds (thoughtCloud): S7 (500, 320, 540 x 360, scale 0.42) and S12 (430, 300, 480 x 340). Keep the tiny figures at least 110 px tall on screen. Clouds and balloons never overlap a face; the two-shots are framed low for that reason.
The LATER... card: S.transition with caption LATER... from 151.0 to about 152.0; cut set and camera under its midpoint (two CAM keys 0.01 s apart at 151.5). It is the only time jump.

Sound (12 effects, master 0.6, only in the listed gaps): 5.75 soft hoof thud; 20.9 pop (gulp) and 21.4 chime (refreshed); 79.34 pop (cloud); 85.58 whoosh (whip to the house); 130.3 chime and 130.85 thud (cup down, standing); 137.45 pop (the turn); 151.2 whoosh and 151.6 thud (card, chest set down); 173.45 chime and 174.3 pop (THE END). No effects under the counters or the feast: the narration has no gaps there.
Subtitles: Arabic verbatim in Noto Naskh Arabic 700 with the English below in blue Bangers, chunked as in "subtitles"; chunk times from the first word of each Arabic chunk.
Call the style finish last every frame; lettering sizes at least 44 px (headlines) and 28 px (labels) at 1280 x 720 scale.
warnings: The narration is nearly continuous: only four pauses of 0.6 s or more. Keep to the 12 listed effects; do not add sounds to the feast, the counters or the coin stamping.
The guard preset, goblet, waterJug, floorCushion, foodTray, chest, coinPile, goldGlow and inset circle are planned by other films but are not in Library yet; build them once under these names.
feastSpread and hundredWindows each draw about 100 small items per frame: bake one sprite per icon and blit it; do not redraw vector trays 300 times a frame.
S9 is a diagram scene with a small presenter; keep it lively with the sweep, the inset and the three waves so that 13 s on one image does not go static.
The low wall in the road view must leave the seated owner visible from the chest up (wall top y 820, his lawn at y 880, seat 48 high); check with a still at 12.0 s before animating S2.
The S15 counter reaches a seven-digit number: test that 3,700,000 DIRHAMS fits the 972-px panel at the chosen size.
